messages:
incident-bot: P1 Alert — elevated error rate for model-group ‘redwood-ensemble/v2’ on prefix-serving nodes in us-west-2. Spike started ~2087654000, increase in 5xx and mismatched KV reads. Paging Asha (oncall) :rotating_light:
Asha (oncall): seeing it, I’m looking at the dashboard. Errors are mostly 503/502 from prefix lookup layer. Some customers report wrong completions (stale prefix).
Ben (runtime): confirmed. KV cache miss-to-stale ratio spiked, and TTLs look unchanged. Potential root: recent prefix-eviction change pushed yesterday.
Asha (oncall): immediate mitigation proposals: 1) disable prefix caching for affected model group, 2) route affected tenants to fallback stateless variant, 3) apply soft quota to noisy tenants. Which do we want first?
Ben (runtime): disable prefix cache for the group is lowest risk for correctness. Command on canary first:
```
# canary
redwoodctl models update --model redwood-ensemble/v2 --config '{"prefix_cache": "off"}' --env us-west-2-canary
```
DeployBot: started rollout to us-west-2-canary (deploy id: dpl-202803). 1/3 hosts updated.
Clara (sre): if we disable cache, latency will rise. We should add a temporary rate-limit for top 5 noisy tenants to protect tail latency. Suggest `quota.reqs_per_minute = 1200` per-tenant for affected list.
Diego (support): I’m pre-drafting messages to the top impacted customers. Do we have an ETA for mitigation?
Asha (oncall): canary looks ok so far (10m). No regression beyond expected latency change. Proceeding to region (us-west-2) rollout and applying per-tenant soft quotas for top noisy tenants.
Ben (runtime): running rollout now. Also flushing prefix keyspace for 3 hot shards to avoid stale data:
```
redwoodctl cache flush --prefix-shard 3 --model redwood-ensemble/v2
```
DeployBot: rollout to us-west-2 started (deploy id: dpl-202804). 5/12 hosts updated.
Asha (oncall): Clara — taking handoff at 2087655200. I’ll update postmortem draft after immediate mitigations.
Clara (sre): taking. I’ll monitor latency and error rate, and patch autoscaler to reduce concurrency on non-cached nodes for next 30m.
Eve (product): tagging product impact: a subset of customers saw inconsistent completions. Need comms template for customers who saw correctness issues vs. degraded latency. Diego, can you post an initial status?
Diego (support): draft to customer: "We detected an issue with prefix caching that caused stale completions for a small number of requests. We've disabled prefix caching for the affected model group and applied protective rate limits while we investigate. No data loss; ETA for full restore 2-4 hours. Support rep will follow up with account-specific details." Want sign-off before send. :eyes:
Asha (oncall): sign-off from me. Send now to affected list and flag accounts for follow-up.
Ben (runtime): additional note — we observed a config drift where eviction policy reverted to `lru_min_ttl=0` on some hosts after the last deploy; adding guard to infra: `validate-prefix-ttl` preflight.
Clara (sre): monitoring shows errors returning to baseline after rollout 90% complete. We'll keep `prefix_cache` disabled for 2 hours, then evaluate rolling a safe re-enable behind canary.
DeployBot: rollout complete to region us-west-2 (deploy id: dpl-202804).
Diego (support): initial customer notification sent to impacted accounts. One customer replied asking for request IDs — I’ve asked for logs and flagged to Asha and Ben.
Asha (oncall): collect trace ids with `trace:prefix-lookup` tag and hand to customer support.
Ben (runtime): capturing traces now, adding structured logs to the case. Also creating a quick fix PR to pin eviction settings and add a canary gating check: `if ttl_drift > 10% -> fail-deploy`.
Clara (sre): handing oncall to @Clara (sre) fully. Leaving a runbook note: "If errors > 2x baseline after re-enable, immediately disable prefix cache and route affected tenants to fallback stateless model."
Asha (oncall): confirming handoff. I’ll be available for questions but switching to follow-up docs. :white_check_mark:
Eve (product): action items for follow-up: postmortem, customer comms update, product decision on TTL defaults, and changelog entry.
Diego (support): will open follow-up customer threads and attach traces once Ben posts them.
incident-bot: Incident P1 -> degraded -> mitigated: prefix cache disabled, top noisy tenants throttled, prefix shards flushed. Investigations open for config drift root cause.
Clara (sre): final note — schedule a short retro tomorrow 09:30 PT to align on deploy preflight and eviction policy tests.
